description:
Lists the scheduled dates of a seminar, soonest first.

Past dates are never returned. Without `from` the window starts today.
`from` and `to` are calendar days in German time, and both are included.
An empty result means nothing is currently scheduled -- it does not mean
the seminar does not exist.

Each date carries the cities it runs in; a city of type `virtual` is an
online delivery, `place` is on site. Dates that are cancelled, postponed
or already over are never returned.

`status` is what to lead with when suggesting a date:

  guaranteed  this seminar runs, whatever else happens -- recommend these
              first, and say so, because it is the customer's strongest
              reason to pick one date over another
  planned     scheduled and open for enrolment, not yet confirmed to run

`direct_booking` appears only on dates that can be booked straight
through the portal, with `direct_booking_until` as the last day for it.
**Its absence says nothing about availability.** Every date listed here
can be enquired about and enrolled in; direct booking is a shortcut, not
a condition. Never tell a customer a date is unavailable because this
field is missing.

`seminar` names the course the dates belong to -- name, duration and
its `url` -- so the list can be presented under that heading. It is
left out only when the lookup failed; the dates still stand.

`begin` and `finish`, per date and per day in `days`, are UTC. The
seminars run in local time (Europe/Berlin; Vienna and Zurich are the
same zone): convert before quoting a time, so 07:00Z is 09:00 in summer
and 08:00 in winter, never "7 Uhr".

city.description: Place name such as "München", or "online" for virtual delivery

from.description: Earliest start date, "YYYY-MM-DD". Defaults to today

name: seminar_dates
title: Get seminar dates
